title: Rick Explains: Monolithic vs Microservices
caption: Why your app's architecture matters! #SoftwareDev

scenes.script: Alright Morty, listen up. You know how you used to play with one big Lego set? That’s a monolithic app—everything stuck together like glue.
Uh, yeah. But what’s wrong with that, Rick? It was fun, right?
It is—until you need to change one piece. Suddenly, you gotta rebuild the whole damn thing! It’s a pain, Morty!
Oh wow… that does sound annoying.
Now imagine breaking your Lego set into smaller kits—each one independent. That’s microservices! Change one kit without touching the others.
Wait, so like when I have separate games for my phone? Each app does its own thing?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty with a dumb looking without understanding.png

scenes.script: Exactly! Microservices communicate via APIs—like tiny messengers passing notes. Way more flexible, Morty.
But what if one app crashes? Does it take down the whole phone?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png

scenes.script: Nope! Fault isolation—just like one game crashing doesn’t affect your others. That’s why Netflix uses microservices, Morty!
But it’s not all sunshine, Morty. Microservices need more planning—like organizing a science fair instead of just showing one project.

scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty evil with a serious looking and a portal gun.png

scenes.script: Monolithic for small apps—like a toaster. Microservices for big systems—like, uh, the whole kitchen! And transitioning? Wubba lubba dub dub, Morty!

topic: What is the difference between monolithic and microservices architecture?
